trans-unit.source: What each kind of person may do here. A role carries a privilege level and a set of permissions; system roles ship with the platform and never change.
Delete this role? This cannot be undone.
The person gets an email with a link to choose a password; nobody types one here.

Why this account is being terminated
This cannot be undone: the person loses access for good.

Who may sign in here, how they sign in, and since when. A suspended account can come back; a terminated one cannot.
Account added. The invitation is on its way.
Every hotel on the platform: its code, where it stands, its rooms, currency and language, and whether it is open for business.
The lists every hotel in Harmony shares: countries, cities, currencies, time zones, languages, property types and the regimes they live under. Kept here by the platform team; a hotel only reads them.
Every table is empty: this is a fresh installation. Start with currencies and time zones, then countries, then the rest; each table checks that the rows it points at already exist.
No rows yet. Add the first one.
The code or key is chosen once and then fixed.
The identity of the row (its code or key) cannot change: other rows point at it.
Untick to retire the row: it stays, because other rows point at it, but is offered to nobody new.
A sentence for the next administrator: what the rows are used for.
Chosen once: a global row belongs to the platform and shows in every hotel; a tenant row stays with its tenant.
The currencies a hotel can price, invoice and pay in. Minor units (2 or 3 decimals) come from the money registry, never typed, so money rounds the same everywhere.
3 letters from the ISO 4217 list, like JOD, SAR or AED. Must be a currency Harmony can price in. Fixed once saved.
As printed on invoices, like Jordanian dinar.
The clocks hotels run on: business date, night audit, check-in time. A city points at one, so a hotel in Jordan can never be saved with a Riyadh clock.
The IANA zone id, Region/City, like Asia/Amman or Asia/Riyadh. One per real zone (Dubai and Muscat share Asia/Dubai). The server must recognise it. Fixed once saved.
What people read in the dropdown, like Amman (Jordan).
The languages guests and staff use: confirmation mails, registration cards and screens come out in them.
2 letters from the ISO 639-1 list, like ar, en or fr. Stored lower-case. Fixed once saved.
The name an administrator reads, like Arabic.
The name in the language itself, what a speaker reads when choosing it: العربية, Français, 日本語.
Written right to left (Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu): screens flip their layout
Where hotels, companies and guests are from. From the country Harmony knows the currency to propose, the regions and cities to offer, the dial code, and later the tax and legal regimes.
2 letters from the ISO 3166-1 list, like JO, SA or AE. Addresses, nationalities and tax rules key on it. Fixed once saved.
The same country in its 3-letter ISO form, like JOR, SAU or ARE: passports, bank files and e-invoicing use this one. Not the currency.
A plus sign and the country digits, like +962 or +966. Phone numbers are stored against it.
What a hotel in this country prices in unless told otherwise. Add the currency first if it is not in the list.
Governorates, regions, emirates, states: the level between a country and its cities. Addresses and reports group by them.
The country this subdivision belongs to. Fixed once saved.
From the ISO 3166-2 list: the country code, a hyphen, then 1 to 3 letters or digits, like JO-AM (Amman) or SA-01 (Riyadh). Fixed once saved.
What this level is called in that country: Governorate, Region, Emirate, State, Province.
Where a hotel stands. A city carries its country, subdivision and time zone, so choosing it fills all three for the hotel.
Fixed once saved: the city id is derived from the country and the English name.
The governorate or region the city is in, from that country's list.
Like Amman or Riyadh. One name per country.
The clock a hotel in this city runs on.
Decimal degrees, -90 to 90 (Amman 31.95). For maps and distances.
What kind of place a property is: hotel, hostel, resort, serviced apartments. A row, so a new type needs no release.
A short fixed code, like Hotel, Hostel or Resort: 2 to 32 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. Fixed once saved.
Position in lists: 1 shows first. Zero or more.
The ways hotels are grouped: by brand, by region, by owner. An exclusive type allows one group per property (one brand per hotel). A system row is one Harmony's own code relies on.
A short fixed code, like Brand, Region or Owner: 2 to 32 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. Fixed once saved.
Exclusive: a property can belong to only one group of this type (one brand per hotel)
System row: Harmony's code relies on it; it can be renamed later but its exclusivity is locked

What a customer subscribes to: per hotel (reservations, POS) or once for the whole customer (loyalty, multi-property). Each service checks subscription lines against these codes, so a code never changes.
What the owning service checks, like pms.core or multi.property: 2 to 32 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. Fixed once saved.
What a salesperson reads, like PMS core or Multiple properties.
The service that enforces it, like Identity, Fiscal or Guest.
Property (one hotel; the subscription line names the hotel and its rooms)
Tenant (once for the whole customer, like loyalty or multi-property)
Hotel modules are sold per property; chain-wide modules to the company.
Has a limit: a subscription line carries a number (rooms, terminals)
The legal, tax, accounting and accommodation regimes a hotel lives under, one row per country and regime. A hotel in Jordan is under JO-GST; the Fiscal service knows what that means.
A short fixed code, usually country and regime, like JO-GST, SA-VAT or JO-LEGAL: 2 to 32 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. Fixed once saved.
The country whose regime this is. Fixed once saved.
Like Jordan general sales tax or Saudi VAT.
The service whose rules this regime stands for: Fiscal for tax and accounting, Identity for legal, Guest for accommodation.
The named lists screens choose from (guest titles, room features, payment reasons): a category is the list, its values are the choices. Global ones show in every hotel.
What the list is called where a screen offers it, like Guest title or Room feature.
The choices inside one category, in the order and words a screen shows them. Choose the category first; retire a value rather than delete it once it has been used.
The list this value belongs to. Fixed once saved.
The words the screen shows, like Mr, Mrs or Sea view.
Untick to retire the value: what was chosen before keeps it; new choices do not see it.

A new invitation goes to this person; leave both empty to send it again to the one already known.
